target.name: Orangewood Labs
target.founder: Abhinav Das, Aditya Bhatia, Akash Bansal

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $10M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
Orangewood Labs is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $5M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 9 private robotics firms and 1 public comparable, representing the frontier-tech robotics subsector at seed through Series B stages.

Two triangulation methods apply here. Stage-progression analysis uses the $10M total-raised proxy as a baseline and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement, yielding an implied valuation of $20M. Peer-median analysis across four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—Generalist AI ($2.0B Series B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B Series B), and Walden Robotics ($1.1B Seed)—produces a median of $1.7B, with a range of $1.1B to $2.0B.

The wide dispersion between methods reflects the substantial stage and maturity heterogeneity within early-stage robotics. Stage-progression implies $20M; peer median implies $1.7B. A conservative triangulated range of $17M to $2.0B with a median of $860M acknowledges both approaches. Key uncertainties include the relevance of Series B peer valuations to an early Series A company, capital efficiency relative to peers, and whether robotics valuations will sustain at current multiples. A more grounded estimate would likely skew toward the lower end absent evidence of outsized technical differentiation or early commercial traction.
